It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and profiled into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Worldia
providers.description: Worldia is a Paris-based B2B2C travel technology company, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Montreuil, France, that lets travel distributors, retailers and agents build, price and book personalized tailor-made trips across more than 80 destinations from a single connected platform. Its product is a white-label trip-building and booking stack — a curated multi-supplier catalogue of accommodations, activities, transfers, car hire, rail and flights, combined with itinerary templates, channel-specific branding and 24/7 traveler support — delivered to each partner as a branded storefront. The platform is driven by a production REST API at api.worldia.com built on API Platform (Symfony) that content-negotiates JSON-LD and Hydra and is multi-tenanted through a required X-Channel header; Worldia publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI or public API reference, so the API is reached through commercial partnership rather than self-service signup.

providers.name: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, Inc. (NYSE: WH) is the world's largest hotel franchising company by number of properties, with over 8,300 affiliated hotels and approximately 869,000 rooms across roughly 25 brands in 95+ countries, licensed to more than 6,200 franchisees. Headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey, its home market is the United States. Wyndham does not operate most of its hotels — it franchises brands (Days Inn, Super 8, Ramada, La Quinta, Microtel, Baymont, Howard Johnson, Travelodge, Wingate, Wyndham, Wyndham Grand, Trademark Collection, TRYP, Dolce, ECHO Suites and others) and sells the demand that flows through them. It sits in the distribution chain as a franchisor and demand aggregator rather than as a distribution platform: inventory reaches buyers through Wyndham's own brand.com sites and Wyndham Rewards, through GDS chain codes under master chain code WR, and through third-party online travel agents, with the central reservation layer supplied by Sabre Hospitality's SynXis CRS under a relationship Sabre publicly renewed in July 2024. There is no travel API: no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, and no property, rate, availability, reservation, loyalty or folio surface is machine-readable anywhere. developer., developers., docs. and api. subdomains do not resolve; /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /api-docs all return 404, and mcp.wyndhamhotels.com resolves with a valid certificate but serves an Akamai 503 on every path. The Terms of Use (effective 2026-03-12) affirmatively prohibit robots, spiders, meta-searching and automated access, and separately prohibit automated access to Wyndham's AI Search. What a second enrichment round did find on 2026-07-28 is undocumented CMS infrastructure that is nonetheless genuinely live: www.wyndhambusiness.com and development.wyndhamhotels.com both run WordPress on WP Engine and leave the WordPress REST API anonymously readable (309 and 403 registered routes, with JSON Schema available by HTTP OPTIONS), and three WordPress MCP adapter routes are registered across the two estates — one of them, on www.wyndhambusiness.com, bound to a real OAuth 2.1 authorization server with RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 discovery metadata, mandatory PKCE S256 and a single `mcp` scope, returning a standards-correct 401 bearer challenge to anonymous callers. None of it is documented, supported, or usable without a credential Wyndham issues to no third party, and none of it carries hotel data. The integration surface that matters is still reached only through a franchise agreement, a commercial distribution agreement, or Sabre.

providers.name: Aescape
providers.description: Aescape is a New York City lifestyle-robotics company, founded in 2017 by Eric Litman, that builds a fully automated AI-powered robotic massage platform. Its table uses sensors and computer vision to map over one million 3D data points of a person's body, then drives heated robotic arms through massage techniques at a user-selected pressure, duration and focus area, with sessions booked and controlled through a mobile/web app. Sessions run 15 to 60 minutes and the tables are deployed in Equinox clubs, Four Seasons, Marriott and Ritz-Carlton properties, spas and corporate wellness sites across North America, alongside an Aescape One home product. Aescape publishes no public developer API: its consumer app is served by a private AWS API Gateway host (api.aescape.com) and its developer documentation site (developer.aescape.com) is gated behind HTTP Basic auth. The one machine-readable, anonymously reachable contract Aescape does publish is the OpenID Connect discovery document for its Zitadel identity tenant.

providers.name: OpenTable
providers.description: OpenTable is a global restaurant reservation platform owned by Booking Holdings. The OpenTable Partner Portal exposes restricted partner APIs for reservations, availability, restaurant content, reviews, and CRM integrations to approved partners.

providers.name: TravelClick (Amadeus)
providers.description: TravelClick, now Amadeus Hospitality, is a hotel commerce and distribution technology provider whose flagship product is the iHotelier Booking Engine 4.0 (CRS/central reservation system). For developers it publishes the Amadeus iHotelier BE API — a family of OAuth 2.0 secured REST APIs that let web and B2C guest-facing applications search availability, hold and create reservations, manage group bookings, and drive the hotel booking flow. TravelClick also operates OTA Connect, a distribution API that connects channel-management partners and OTAs to hotel inventory. API documentation and interactive testing are available to accounts registered on the developer portal at developer.travelclick.com; non-production API keys are issued on request.

providers.name: Joy (ex-Privateaser)
providers.description: Joy is a French SaaS platform for bars, restaurants and venues that turns group and event enquiries into confirmed bookings. Founded in 2014 as Privateaser, the company now runs a two-sided business: privateaser.com, the group-venue marketplace that captures demand, and Joy, the manager-facing application (web plus iOS/Android) where an establishment centralises requests from Google, Instagram, its own website, WhatsApp and Privateaser, then works them through a unified calendar and messaging inbox, an SEO/GEO-optimised event showcase page, a virtual phone assistant, quotes, French-compliant invoicing, and Stripe-backed deposits and prepayments. Joy reports more than 3,000 partner establishments and over EUR100M in bookings managed in 2025. It publishes no public API, SDK, webhook catalogue or developer portal; the only integration surfaces it documents for customers are an embeddable iframe booking form, Reserve-with-Google, and a one-click reservation copy into Zenchef.

providers.name: Laundryheap
providers.description: Laundryheap is a London-founded on-demand laundry and dry-cleaning company that collects, cleans and returns clothing within 24 hours, operating across the United Kingdom, United States, Ireland, the Netherlands, Sweden, Denmark, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Singapore. It serves consumers directly through iOS, Android and web apps, and businesses through hotel-affiliate, commercial laundry and dry-cleaning partner programmes. Laundryheap operates no developer portal and publishes no API documentation, but it does run a real, live, standards-clean OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect authorization server on its own root host — complete with PKCE, token introspection, token revocation and open dynamic client registration — advertising an `orders.create` scope, alongside a production GraphQL API of 69 fields and a small unauthenticated JSON endpoint that returns its service catalogue. The API surface is real and substantial; what is missing is any documentation of it.

providers.name: 2ndKitchen
providers.description: 2ndKitchen was a Chicago-based food-technology startup (Techstars '18) that let businesses without an on-site kitchen — bars, breweries, hotels, and apartment communities — offer custom food menus sourced from nearby partner restaurants, handling ordering, pricing, payment, and delivery on their behalf. The company was acquired by REEF Technology in December 2021 and its 2ndkitchen.com domain now redirects to reeftechnology.com. This API Evangelist profile captures the set of nine microservice OpenAPI definitions still published on the legacy Swagger UI at docs.2ndkitchen.com (authentication, business, user, restaurant, order, pricing, payment, delivery, and indexing services), preserved here as a historical record of the platform's API surface.

providers.name: eZee Technosys
providers.description: eZee Technosys is a hospitality technology company offering eZee Absolute (cloud hotel PMS), eZee Centrix (channel manager), eZee Reservation (booking engine), and eZee Optimus (restaurant POS). Its YCS Connectivity Portal exposes a partner-gated HTTP API for PMS connectivity, channel manager, booking engine, and POS integrations so third-party systems can sync reservations, room inventory, rates, restrictions, and guest data. eZee is now part of Yanolja Cloud (Yanolja Cloud Solution).

providers.name: Atmosphere
providers.description: Atmosphere (Atmosphere TV) is an Austin, Texas streaming television platform built for businesses rather than households. Spun out of Chive Media Group (theCHIVE) in 2019, it delivers free, ad-supported, audio-optional short-form channels - CHIVE TV, Atmosphere Sports, Happy TV, Nostalgia TV and partner channels - to bars, restaurants, gyms and health clubs, hotels, airports, medical waiting rooms, salons, casinos and other out-of-home venues over a streaming player and Android TV app. Alongside the channel lineup it sells a digital-signage product for venue-owned promotions, Atmosphere Trivia for in-venue engagement, a Business Manager mobile app for controlling screens, and an advertising network that monetizes those venue screens as connected-TV and digital-out-of-home inventory. Atmosphere raised a $65M Series D in February 2023 at a $1B valuation led by Sageview Capital with Valor Equity Partners and S3 Ventures. Atmosphere publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; api.atmosphere.tv is an undocumented first-party backend serving its own apps and venue console, and its shares trade on the private secondary market.

providers.name: Hireology
providers.description: Hireology is a purpose-built applicant tracking system (ATS) and hiring platform for multi-location, high-volume employers, with deep specialization in retail automotive, healthcare (including long-term and home care), and hospitality. The platform spans the full hiring lifecycle — candidate sourcing and job distribution, applicant engagement and texting, structured screening and skills assessments, interview and evaluation workflows, hiring decisions, and onboarding handoff — plus reporting and analytics that help operators hire consistently, faster, and at scale across locations. Hireology integrates with payroll, HRIS, background-check, scheduling, and job-board partners such as ADP, UKG, BambooHR, Indeed, CDK, Dealertrack, and Accurate. It maintains a SOC 2 Type II program and a public Trust Center. Hireology does not publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI specification; integrations are delivered through named partner connectors. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures.

providers.name: Tabit
providers.description: Tabit is a mobile-first, cloud-based restaurant point-of-sale and hospitality management platform from Tabit Technologies. Its product suite spans tableside mobile ordering and payments (PAD/Pay), online ordering (Order), kitchen display (Chef), self-service kiosks, delivery (Wheels), guest management, gift cards, and hotel F&B/PMS integration. Tabit does not publish a public, self-service developer API or API reference; integrations are delivered through a partner program and an integration-request process rather than an open developer portal.

providers.name: Kitopi
providers.description: Kitopi is a Dubai-headquartered, tech-powered multi-brand restaurant and cloud kitchen platform that discovers, creates and curates homegrown F&B brands for the MENA region. It operates over 200 restaurant and delivery-only outlets across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and Kuwait with more than 6,000 employees, and runs a Global Customer Experience center in Dubai plus a 100-plus person technology hub in Krakow, Poland. Kitopi's differentiator is its in-house Smart Kitchen Operating System (SKOS), a suite of applications that optimizes every aspect of cloud-kitchen operations in real time to maximize throughput and utilization for its restaurant partners, letting a brand scale into a new market in roughly 14 days. Kitopi is a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company. It publishes no public product or partner developer API; its only machine-readable surface is a Wix-provided site MCP endpoint and an llms.txt agent-access declaration on www.kitopi.com.

providers.name: Elyra
providers.description: Elyra is an AI-powered restaurant operations and reservation platform, backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026 batch) and founded in Stockholm by Felix Odeberg Glasenapp and Alan Mando. The product combines an AI voice agent that answers reservation phone calls, an email concierge that handles confirmations and follow-ups, guest intelligence that builds diner profiles from preferences and booking history, smart table-allocation and walk-in optimization, plus analytics and campaign outreach tooling. It serves restaurant groups primarily across Scandinavia, addressing the roughly 40% of incoming calls restaurants miss and the booking delays that follow. Elyra operates as a business-facing SaaS application at app.elyrasystems.com and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Aloha POS
providers.description: Aloha POS is a restaurant point-of-sale platform from NCR Voyix. The NCR Voyix Developer Experience exposes APIs for Aloha (cloud and on-premise) covering site, store, menu, order, payment, and reporting integrations as part of the broader NCR Voyix Commerce Platform.

providers.name: Evolve
providers.description: Evolve (formerly Evolve Vacation Rental) is a Denver, Colorado hospitality company founded in 2011 that manages more than 30,000 short-term rental properties across the United States, Canada, Mexico and the Caribbean. It runs a hybrid vacation-rental management model: Evolve handles listing creation, photography, dynamic pricing, marketing, distribution to Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, Google, Hopper and Homes & Villas by Marriott Bonvoy, guest communication and 24/7 support, while the owner keeps the freedom to choose their own on-the-ground cleaning and service providers. Owners pick a Core, Plus or Pro management plan; guests book directly at evolve.com. Evolve publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract — it consumes channel-manager APIs rather than publishing one. Its distribution integration platform is built on AWS (API Gateway, S3, Aurora) with Rentals United as the channel manager.

providers.name: Hostfully
providers.description: Hostfully is a San Francisco-based short-term rental (STR) property management platform serving vacation rental managers, property managers, and hospitality operators worldwide. The Hostfully Property Management Platform (PMP) provides a channel manager that syncs listings across 60+ booking channels including Airbnb, Vrbo, and Booking.com (where Hostfully holds preferred/elite partner status), a central calendar, unified inbox with InboxAI for guest communication, direct booking site builder, automation and task management, multi-unit and group-booking management, payment processing via Stripe/PayPal/VRP, owner portal, mobile apps for iOS and Android, and digital guidebooks. The platform manages 62,000+ properties for 40,000+ customers, processing 96,000+ bookings monthly. Hostfully exposes a developer-grade public REST API (v3.3) and a GraphQL API for partners and property managers, supporting OAuth 2.0 authorization-code, basic auth, and X-HOSTFULLY-APIKEY authentication, cursor-based pagination, webhooks for agency/booking/property/messaging/custom-data events, and a 10,000 calls/hour per-client rate limit. The API is offered as an add-on across the Growth, Pro, and Enterprise Property Management Software plans.

providers.name: MenuSifu
providers.description: MenuSifu is a U.S. restaurant technology company founded in 2014 that builds an all-in-one point-of-sale and restaurant operations platform, used by more than 15,000 active restaurants and supported from offices in New York, Los Angeles, Houston, Orlando, Silicon Valley and Chicago. The platform spans POS terminals and handhelds, self-service kiosks, kitchen display and kitchen-automation systems, electronic menus and order-status screens, online ordering, scan-to-order, waitlist and reservations, loyalty, coupons and SMS marketing, and analytics and reporting, with direct order integrations into DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Fantuan and HungryPanda. It is sold alongside an ecosystem of sibling brands — USEZPAY (payment processing), MealKeyway (marketing), EZ Capital (restaurant financing), WeFood and ShowTop. MenuSifu markets no public developer program: it publishes no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, and no SDKs, and its production host api.menusifu.com rejects every anonymous request.

providers.name: WOW! Momo
providers.description: WOW! Momo Foods Private Limited is the Kolkata, India quick-service restaurant company founded in August 2008 by St. Xavier's College alumni Sagar J. Daryani and Binod K. Homagai, which built a national chain around the momo and now operates three brands — WOW! Momo, WOW! China and WOW! Chicken (launched December 2021) — across roughly 650 outlets in more than 30 Indian cities, backed by Lighthouse Funds, Tiger Global, Khazanah Nasional and Oaks Capital. WOW! Momo runs no developer programme: it publishes no API documentation, developer portal, SDK, API pricing or support channel, and no company-authored OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL contract exists anywhere public. It is catalogued here because www.wowmomo.com serves a live, anonymously readable WordPress REST API — advertised in the head of every page as <link rel="https://api.w.org/"> — exposing the site's pages, media library, taxonomies, search index, oEmbed 1.0 provider endpoint and Yoast SEO head document, alongside a separate first-party application backend on api.wowmomo.com that answers every anonymous request, including a control path that cannot exist, with an identical NO_AUTH body.

providers.name: Garten
providers.description: garten (styled lowercase; formerly Oh My Green) is a workplace food and wellbeing company founded in 2014 by Michael Heinrich and backed by Y Combinator, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. It runs turn-key office micro-kitchens and pantries (garten Kitchen), self-serve micro-markets with cashless checkout kiosks (garten Market), corporate catering and cafe management (garten Catering), and virtual and on-site wellbeing programming (garten Wellbeing, plus the garten TV streaming property), serving employers including Google, Nike, Ford and Autodesk across roughly twenty US metros. garten was acquired by the chef-driven catering platform HUNGRY in 2025. garten publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable REST contract: its client ordering surface at client.garten.co / api.garten.co is a credentialed Spree/Solidus commerce application whose API rejects anonymous calls with "You must specify an API key." The one genuinely public, machine-readable agent surface sits on its Uscreen-powered streaming property garten TV (tv.garten.co), which serves a Model Context Protocol server at /mcp guarded by a full OAuth 2.1 stack: RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata, PKCE S256, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, RFC 8707 resource indicators, and seven named read/write scopes.

providers.name: Table22
providers.description: Table22 is a subscription commerce and growth platform built specifically for food & beverage businesses. It enables restaurants, wine shops, wineries, butchers, bakeries, specialty grocers, and retailers to launch and grow subscriptions, clubs, memberships, pre-orders, and product drops that generate predictable recurring revenue beyond their four walls. The full-service platform combines branded storefronts, an order management system, white-glove fulfillment coordination, automated lifecycle marketing and CRM, five-star consumer support, and AI tools for hospitality. Over 1,000 merchants across 40 U.S. states use Table22, representing $100M+ in revenue impact. Pricing is success-based (15% revenue share, no upfront or setup fees). Table22 is a sales-led SaaS with no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, website surface, and machine-readable llms.txt.

providers.name: SynergySuite
providers.description: SynergySuite is a back-of-house restaurant management platform for multi-unit and enterprise restaurant operators, founded in 2011 and operating across the United States, United Kingdom and Ireland. The suite covers inventory and purchasing, recipe and food costing, food safety and HACCP checklists, labor scheduling, cash management, human resources and business intelligence, delivered through a web interface and mobile applications. Its operational value depends on integration: SynergySuite ingests sales and order data from point-of-sale platforms including Toast, PAR Brink, NCR Aloha, Appetize by SpotOn and Oracle MICROS Simphony, and exchanges data with accounting, payroll, supplier and HR systems over POS integrations, EDI and data services. That integration surface is operated as a first-class product — it is monitored as named components on the company status page — but the API contract and reference are distributed through a partner portal that requires a login rather than a public developer site.

providers.name: Dayuse
providers.description: Dayuse is a global online marketplace for daytime hotel bookings, letting travelers reserve 3-to-5-star hotel rooms by the hour or for a microstay during the day rather than for an overnight stay, at discounts of up to 75% off the nightly rate. Founded in France in 2010, the platform connects consumers with more than 9,000 partner hotels across roughly 29 countries, with use cases spanning remote work, layovers, wellness and spa access, and privacy. Hoteliers join through the Dayuse partner network and manage daytime inventory via the partner portal. Dayuse is backed by Partech and is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API is currently published, so this profile captures identity, partner surface, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Tebi
providers.description: Tebi is a hospitality management platform that unifies point-of-sale, payments, and back-office operations for restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, quick-service venues, and events. The system connects front-of-house service to back-office administration in a single product spanning Point of Sale, Kitchen Display System, Reservations, integrated card Payments (with invoicing and split-bill), QR ordering, inventory management, CRM, recipe management, and AI-driven insights. Tebi is priced on a revenue-based subscription (the first EUR 10k of monthly revenue is free, each additional EUR 10k costs EUR 20/month) with no long-term contracts, and it bundles its own payment processing with transparent per-transaction fees. The company is backed by Index Ventures. Tebi does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its production identity, help center, changelog, status page, and security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Canary Technologies
providers.description: Canary Technologies is an AI-powered hospitality management platform trusted by more than 20,000 hotels across 90+ countries, including brands such as Marriott International, Four Seasons, Choice Hotels, Wyndham, and IHG. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in San Francisco, Canary provides digital guest management — contactless mobile check-in/checkout, tablet registration, upsells, guest messaging, digital tipping, and Canary AI — along with PCI-compliant secure transactions and fraud prevention. The company maintains its own integration tooling and a partner/enterprise API that connects to 80+ property-management, payment, and hospitality systems (Oracle Hospitality, Mews, Cloudbeds, Sabre, Adyen, Shift4, and others), launching 5-10 new integrations per quarter. Canary does not publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI; API access is granted to hotel partners and integration providers.

providers.name: Slang Ai
providers.description: Slang AI is a voice-AI phone-answering and reservation platform for restaurants. Its customizable virtual phone agent answers every inbound call 24/7 in a natural, human-like voice, instantly responds to guest inquiries, and automatically manages reservations, with official integrations to OpenTable, SevenRooms, Tripleseat, Yelp, and Fishbowl. Founded by former Spotify data scientists, Slang AI reports 96%+ guest satisfaction (CSAT), 50% more phone reservations, and up to 200 staff hours saved per month. It is offered as a hosted SaaS product across Core, Premium, and Enterprise plans; at the time of profiling it exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Blueground
providers.description: Blueground is a global proptech company that leases, furnishes and operates move-in-ready apartments for stays of a month or longer, running thousands of units across cities in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America. It operates an end-to-end technology stack: a consumer booking site and iOS/Android guest apps, an internal property, pricing and operations platform, and the Blueground Partner Network — an invite-only marketplace where third-party furnished-rental operators list supply and connect inventory through PMS and channel-manager integrations (Avantio, NextPax, Rentals United, Hostify, Hostfully, SiteMinder, Cloudbeds, Airbnb). Blueground publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable contract: partner connectivity is brokered through channel-manager partners rather than a self-serve API. Its engineering organization does maintain a real open-source footprint on GitHub (bluegroundltd), with libraries released to Maven Central and npm, and the main website publishes an llms.txt.

providers.name: Boompop
providers.description: Boompop is a corporate event management and planning SaaS platform that helps companies organize offsites, conferences, team gatherings, and other business events. The platform pairs AI-powered planning tools that generate briefs, agendas, and logistics with hotel and vendor sourcing (AI-powered RFPs and rate negotiation), guest and RSVP management, itinerary and event websites, budget and expense tracking, and 24/7 AI messaging. Tiers range from a free Starter plan through a per-event Pro plan to Full Service white-glove planning with a dedicated expert. Boompop was named the 7th fastest-growing software company on the 2025 Inc. 5000 list. It is SOC 2 certified and GDPR compliant, and offers passwordless login plus Google and Microsoft single sign-on. Boompop is backed by Wing Venture Capital. Boompop does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Resy
providers.description: Resy is a restaurant reservation and discovery platform owned by American Express. Resy does not maintain a publicly self-serve developer portal; integration is restricted to approved partners (POS, CRM, loyalty, marketing, and discovery) under direct partnership agreements. The primary public surface is the consumer web and mobile app and an embeddable "Book with Resy" booking widget for restaurants. The unofficial internal client API at api.resy.com has been widely reverse-engineered by the community, but it is undocumented, unsupported, and may change without notice.

providers.name: Food Market Hub
providers.description: Food Market Hub is a cloud-based procurement, inventory, and supply-chain management platform for food-and-beverage businesses, founded in Malaysia and headquartered in Petaling Jaya, Selangor. It automates back-end operations for restaurants, cafes, and central kitchens — connecting F&B outlets with their suppliers and central kitchens to handle purchase-order creation, smart ordering, inventory tracking, food-cost and wastage control, supplier management, and real-time reporting. The platform serves brands such as KFC, Pizza Hut, Salad Atelier, and Kenny Hills alongside thousands of independent restaurants across Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Indonesia, and China), and is delivered through web and iOS/Android mobile apps. Food Market Hub is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; integrations (including POS sales-data connections) are handled directly by the company.

providers.name: CAVA
providers.description: CAVA Group, Inc. (NYSE: CAVA) is a Washington, D.C.-headquartered Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant company that operates the CAVA brand, serving customizable bowls, pitas, salads and sides built on house-made dips, spreads and dressings. Alongside its restaurants CAVA runs a consumer packaged goods line sold in grocery stores, a digital ordering and delivery channel, a catering business at catering.cava.com, and the CAVA Rewards loyalty program delivered through its iOS and Android apps. The company listed on the New York Stock Exchange in June 2023 and reports an in-house technology program — CavaCore, its data platform, and CAVA Current, a restaurant operating system. CAVA publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public machine-readable surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt and a published llms.txt.

providers.name: BevSpot
providers.description: BevSpot is a Boston-based food and beverage inventory management platform for restaurants, bars, and hospitality groups. The web application streamlines back-of-house operations including inventory counting, ordering, invoice management, recipe and menu costing, and sales-driven analytics. BevSpot ingests point-of-sale data through integrations with more than a dozen POS systems (Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed, SpotOn, NCR Aloha, Upserve, Brink, Lavu, and others), plus accounting and vendor connections (QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics GP, Ottimate, Fintech, US Foods, Sysco). It is a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures. BevSpot does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, commercial, and security surface.

providers.name: FineDine
providers.description: FineDine is an AI-powered restaurant growth platform that helps restaurants increase revenue through digital menus (QR code, tablet, and web), online and in-venue ordering, reservations, a lite point-of-sale, CRM and loyalty programs, menu-engineering and pricing analytics, and an AI business agent (FineDine IQ). It markets to restaurants and hospitality operators with tiered SaaS pricing (Starter, Growth, Premium). As of this API Evangelist profiling, FineDine publishes no public developer API, SDKs, webhooks, CLI, MCP server, or OpenAPI specification — this profile captures its public commercial and content surface. FineDine is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: HostnFly
providers.description: HostnFly is a French short-term-rental (Airbnb) concierge and property-management company, founded in 2016 and headquartered in Paris. It manages the full lifecycle of short-stay rentals on behalf of property owners: listing creation and optimization, multi-platform distribution (Airbnb, Booking.com, Abritel), guest screening and 24/7 communication, check-in/check-out and key handling, hotel-grade housekeeping and linen, maintenance, short-term-rental insurance, and dynamic revenue optimization. HostnFly operates on a commission-only model (from ~20% of nightly revenue, no fixed fees) and covers 340+ cities across metropolitan France and Corsica. It is a Partech portfolio company. HostnFly publishes an llms.txt agent-discovery file but does not expose a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Tillpoint
providers.description: Tillpoint is a modular, cloud-based EPOS (electronic point of sale) and business management platform for retail, hospitality, and services. A single subscription bundles 25+ modules - Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers/CRM, Staff, Accounting, Purchase Orders, Reporting, and more - across one terminal or thousands of locations. As of this review Tillpoint does not publish a documented public or partner developer API - there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no OpenAPI. Connectivity is delivered through pre-built integrations (QuickBooks Online, Xero, WooCommerce, PayPal, Worldpay, Mailchimp). The API surfaces catalogued here (Point of Sale, Inventory, Customers, Accounting) are logical capability areas of the platform and are honestly marked as endpointsModeled - no endpoints are fabricated. Direct/programmatic access requires contacting Tillpoint.

providers.name: Gronda
providers.description: Gronda is a professional community and learning platform for chefs and hospitality professionals, offering 70+ masterclasses and 20,000+ exclusive restaurant recipes from leading chefs, a chef directory and creator program, and team and culinary-school plans. Members share culinary creations, follow world-class chefs, and access PRO subscription content through the Gronda web and mobile apps. Backed by Speedinvest, Gronda was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; it is a consumer/community product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Hostie
providers.description: Hostie is an AI-powered virtual concierge for restaurants that answers every call, text, email, and message in the restaurant's own voice so operators never miss a guest and staff can stay focused on in-room service. The conversational AI platform handles phone volume, captures reservations and takeout orders, fields private-event inquiries, and unifies guest communication across calls, texts, emails, Instagram, and Google Maps, with live call transcripts, multilingual support (20 languages), guest history, and data ownership. Restaurant partners include Tonchin, Trader Vic's, Flour + Water, The Slanted Door Group, and The Stinking Rose Group. Hostie raised a $12M Series A led by Obvious Ventures (July 2026), bringing total funding to $16M. Hostie is a business SaaS product and does not currently publish a public API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio tracking.

providers.name: Limehome
providers.description: Limehome is a Munich-headquartered digital hospitality operator founded in 2018 that designs, leases and runs fully-equipped design apartments and aparthotels across Europe, from Berlin to Barcelona and Linz to Lecce. The company runs a 100% digital guest journey: guests browse and book units online, receive an access code, and complete check-in and check-out contactlessly with no on-site reception staff. Limehome operates offices in Munich and Madrid with more than 200 employees, is led by CEOs Dr. Josef Vollmayr and Cesar de Sousa Freitas, and is backed by Picus Capital, HV Capital and Lakestar. Revenue comes from direct bookings (fee-free, with a 15% membership discount) alongside a "Lease to Limehome" real-estate partnership model. Limehome runs a production API host at api.limehome.com behind AWS API Gateway, but publishes no public developer portal, documentation or machine-readable specification; that surface is first-party/private. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization with a small number of open-source engineering libraries, and an engineering blog.

providers.name: Enplug
providers.description: Enplug is a cloud-based digital signage and content-management platform that powers communications on screens across retail, hospitality, corporate, and public-venue locations, with content apps for social feeds, dashboards, video, wayfinding, and menus managed from a central web dashboard. Enplug was acquired by Spectrio, and enplug.com now redirects to Spectrio's Enplug acquisition page; the legacy Enplug cloud login remains live at login.enplug.com. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; Enplug exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this repo carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: FLYR Labs
providers.description: FLYR (formerly FLYR Labs) is a San Francisco-headquartered travel technology company, founded in 2013, that builds an AI-native commercial operating system for airlines, cargo carriers and hospitality operators. Its airline portfolio spans the Cirrus Revenue Operating System (deep-learning forecasting, dynamic pricing and revenue management) and an Offer & Order Management System built on IATA open standards — NDC and ONE Order — with a certified NDC+ API, an NDC Gateway for indirect and B2B channels (GDS, OTAs), and a Legacy Translator for backward compatibility with existing PSS estates. Its hospitality arm, FLYR Hospitality (built on the acquired Pace Revenue platform), ships Optimize, Insights, Planning and Groups to 2,300+ properties with native two-way integrations into property management systems including Mews, Oracle OPERA Cloud, Apaleo, Cloudbeds, RMS Cloud, Stayntouch and Planet/Protel. FLYR has raised over $500M and employs more than 700 people. Its APIs are commercial and partner-gated: the developer portal at developer.flyr.com requires an account, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or GraphQL schema is published to anonymous callers.

providers.name: Hipcamp
providers.description: Hipcamp is the #1 app to find and book campsites globally, with real-time availability across more than 500,000 sites in the United States, Canada, Australia, and the United Kingdom. Campers search national parks, state parks, RV resorts, and private land stays (farms, ranches, vineyards) in one app, with filters, Pro map layers (BLM/USFS land, cell coverage, dark skies), road-trip search, and free availability alerts. Hosts list and manage campsites, sync calendars, and take weekly payouts. Hipcamp integrates with campground reservation systems (ResNexus, Cloudbeds, Newbook, RMS, Bedful) but publishes no public developer API — /api and /graphql are internal-only. Surfaced as an a16z / Bond Capital / Slow Ventures portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: HUNGRY
providers.description: HUNGRY (Hungry Marketplace, Inc.) is an Arlington, Virginia workplace food platform that connects corporate clients to a curated network of independent chefs and local restaurants. Founded in 2016 by Jeff Grass, Eman Pahlavani and Shy Pahlevani, it operates four product lines — office catering, Group Order individual meal pre-ordering, live events and chef pop-ups, and snacks and pantry — plus HUNGRY Last Mile, its own delivery and logistics arm. The platform runs its own admin, chef/food-partner dashboard, client admin dashboard, ops captain app and consumer ordering marketplace across 24 US cities and, following the February 2026 merger with Toronto-based hungerhub, more than ten Canadian markets. Earlier acquisitions include NatureBox and Garten. HUNGRY publishes no public developer program: the backing API at api.tryhungry.com is a private first-party service for its own web and mobile clients, and no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, SDK or partner API reference is published anywhere on its public surface. The company does publish a dated, public engineering release-notes site, which is the only machine-adjacent technical artifact it makes available.

providers.name: Tripitaca, Inc.
providers.description: Tripitaca is a Kenya-based travel and hospitality booking marketplace where travelers get the best deals when they travel and where property owners list their properties. The platform lets travelers receive offers from hosts and hotels, while hosts create curated packages and special offers, see travelers interested in their area, and make them offers. Coverage spans destinations including Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Kisumu, and Maasai Mara safari experiences. Backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Minoan
providers.description: Minoan is a hospitality procurement and shoppable-stays platform. Short-term-rental hosts, property managers, hotels, and interior designers source furniture, decor, and home goods at insider/trade pricing through Minoan's purchasing platform, and earn revenue share when guests buy the items they experienced during a stay. Founded to turn every hosted space into a shoppable showroom, Minoan connects properties to hundreds of home-and-lifestyle brands and handles sourcing, checkout, and fulfillment. Backed by Accel. As of this profile Minoan exposes no public developer API; this record captures its public web, security, and llms.txt surface.

providers.name: Duetto Research
providers.description: Duetto Research is a hospitality technology company whose cloud platform, marketed as Duetto, delivers a Revenue & Profit Operating System (RP-OS) for hotels, casinos, and resorts. The platform pairs real-time dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, group and block business management, and profitability benchmarking so revenue teams can optimize rates and total property profit across more than 20,000 properties in over 100 countries. Its marquee products include GameChanger (dynamic pricing and rate optimization), ScoreBoard (forecasting and reporting), BlockBuster (group business), Advance (AI-driven rate recommendations), GameTime (select-service revenue management), and HotStats (profitability benchmarking). Duetto connects with the property management systems, booking engines, and channel managers hotels already use through a large partner-integration ecosystem rather than a self-serve public developer API. Backed by Battery Ventures; surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: HomeToGo
providers.description: HomeToGo is the world's largest marketplace and search engine for vacation rentals, aggregating roughly 20 million offers from thousands of providers worldwide across cabins, condos, houses, and apartments. Its B2B segment, HomeToGo_PRO, powers the supply side of travel with SaaS and tech-enabled services for individual hosts, property managers, and agencies. Through its Doppelgänger program HomeToGo offers partners multiple integration surfaces — API, White Label, Travel Agency Hub, ad placement, and pop-under — to embed its vacation-rental inventory. HomeToGo is a publicly listed company (Frankfurt Stock Exchange) and a portfolio company of Insight Partners. It does not publish a public, self-serve API specification; API access is arranged through its partner and supply programs.

providers.name: Ciao
providers.description: Ciao (meetciao.com) is a home-sharing platform that connects travelers with locals, letting members rent homes at local rates within a private, trust-based community of travellers while homeowners earn income from their properties. The service emphasizes affordability, community trust, and authentic local experiences over commercial short-let alternatives, and operates across major European cities including London, Lisbon, Berlin, Amsterdam, Paris, and Tbilisi with 20,000+ community members and 1,000+ available homes. Ciao is a Seedcamp portfolio company; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Ciao is a consumer mobile/web product and publishes no public API, developer portal, or specifications at this time.

providers.name: Gathern
providers.description: Gathern (جاذر) is the first licensed peer-to-peer vacation-rental marketplace in Saudi Arabia, founded in Riyadh in 2016 and licensed by the Saudi Ministry of Tourism. Through its iOS, Android, and web apps, travelers book short-term private accommodations directly from local hosts — chalets, apartments, villas, farms, resorts, rest houses (istrahat), camps, caravans, and rooms — across more than 200 cities and provinces in the Kingdom, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Taif, Al Khobar, Dammam, Mecca, Medina, and AlUla. The platform lists tens of thousands of units, has served more than five million users, and holds a leading share of the alternative-hospitality sector in Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, STV, Sanabil Investments (a Public Investment Fund subsidiary), and others, Gathern raised a $72M Series B and is preparing for a Tadawul listing. Gathern operates as a consumer marketplace app and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GigFinesse
providers.description: GigFinesse is a live-entertainment talent booking platform that connects hospitality venues — hotels, restaurants, bars, and clubs — with musicians, DJs, and performing artists. Venues discover and book vetted talent and manage contracts, insurance, scheduling, and payments through a centralized dashboard, while artists gain access to consistent, recurring gig opportunities. Clients include premium hospitality brands such as St. Regis, The Ritz-Carlton, Fairmont Hotels, and Hard Rock Hotel. GigFinesse is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Inspirato
providers.description: Inspirato is a luxury travel subscription company that gives members access to a curated portfolio of 300+ private branded residences, 200+ five-star hotels, and 170+ destinations worldwide, paired with dedicated concierge care, curated experiences, and signature hotel partnerships. Members book vacations through Inspirato's website and app with predictable, service-first delivery. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of IVP and added to the API Evangelist network. Inspirato does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Provi
providers.description: Provi is a B2B beverage alcohol marketplace that digitizes procurement across the three-tier distribution system, connecting buyers (bars, restaurants, and retail stores) with distributors, sales representatives, and suppliers/brands. The platform consolidates product discovery across distributor catalogs, direct messaging with sales reps, order management and processing, and brand showcase tools into a single ordering experience. Provi was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Tab
providers.description: Tab (tab.travel) is a London-based payment platform built specifically for independent tourism and hospitality businesses — hotels, hostels, tour operators, retreat centers and activity providers. It lets these merchants take card payments wherever their guests are, from in-advance deposits and online booking pages to in-person, on-the-move transactions via a mobile app, and to plug into an existing booking engine, PMS or OTA ecosystem. Tab natively handles 140+ currencies, pays out weekly in the merchant's local currency, and advertises transparent pricing from 2.9% per transaction with no hidden fees. Founded in 2015 by Mark Datta and backed by Y Combinator (W2015), Tab also operates a consumer-facing social-commerce guide for discovering and booking travel. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; Tab does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs or API documentation.

providers.name: HEDNA
providers.description: HEDNA (Hotel Electronic Distribution Network Association) is a not-for-profit trade association founded in 1991 and headquartered in Forest Hill, Maryland, United States, that convenes the hotel distribution industry — hotel chains, GDS operators, OTAs, switches, channel managers, payment providers and connectivity vendors — around shared best practice for hospitality electronic distribution. It sits alongside rather than inside the distribution chain: it moves no inventory and processes no bookings, but its Disciplines (Connectivity, Content Distribution, Payments, Data & Analytics, Revenue Optimization) produce recommendation documents, and it co-authored the Open Payments Alliance Standards Specification with HTNG and OpenTravel. HEDNA publishes no developer portal, no API, and no machine-readable specification on hedna.org; every probe of developer./developers./docs./api. subdomains and of /developers, /api, /docs, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ failed (DNS failure or HTTP 404). Its publications library, research reports and HEDNA U courseware are gated behind paid membership at members.hedna.org (HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge unauthenticated) and pathlms.com/hedna. Honest posture: member-gated documents, no public API, no exit path published.

providers.name: Emtethal
providers.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: IHG Hotels & Resorts
providers.description: InterContinental Hotels Group PLC (trading as IHG Hotels & Resorts) is a British asset-light hotel group headquartered at Windsor Dials, 1 Arthur Road, Windsor, Berkshire SL4 1RS, United Kingdom, with an Americas office at 3 Ravinia Drive, Atlanta, Georgia. Its own corporate site states 7,014 hotels and 1,035,589 rooms across more than 100 countries, around 400,000 colleagues, 20 brands and the IHG One Rewards loyalty programme (figures read from ihgplc.com on 2026-07-28). The brand portfolio spans Six Senses, Regent, InterContinental, Vignette Collection, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo, voco, HUALUXE, Crowne Plaza, EVEN Hotels, Holiday Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Holiday Inn Resorts, Holiday Inn Club Vacations, Garner, avid, Atwell Suites, Staybridge Suites, Candlewood Suites, IHG Army Hotels and Iberostar Beachfront Resorts. In the distribution chain IHG sits on the supply side as a franchisor and manager rather than an owner: it aggregates independently owned and operated properties into a single central reservation system and pushes that inventory out through its own ihg.com and app direct channels, through the three GDSs and their agency terminals, through OTAs and wholesalers, and through corporate and group channels. Critically, IHG does not run its own reservation platform any more. It announced a partnership with Amadeus in 2015 to build a cloud Guest Reservation System to replace HOLIDEX, its proprietary system in service since 1965, and migrated onto it across 2018 and early 2019 — so the hotel group most likely to be a lock-in vendor is itself a customer of a GDS company's platform, and group bookings land in Amadeus Delphi and Meeting Broker. Its API posture, stated honestly, is gated and undocumented. There is no live developer portal. The one that existed — PartnerConnect RoomService at pcroomservice.ihg.com, a TIBCO Mashery portal publishing five rate, availability and hotel-content APIs — is decommissioned: the hostname is NXDOMAIN on Google, Cloudflare and Quad9 resolvers as of 2026-07-28 and the Internet Archive holds no page capture after 2019. What remains live is partnerconnect.ihg.com (HTTP 200), an affiliate marketing programme whose signup routes to Commission Junction and which still advertises "access to real-time hotel rates, availability and hotel content API's" without linking to any technical resource. Real API hostnames exist — api.ihg.com CNAMEs to ihg.api.mashery.com with an sb-ihg.mashery.com sandbox, and apis.ihg.com, b2b.ihg.com, mcp.ihg.com, booking.ihg.com and concerto.ihg.com all sit behind Akamai — but every one returns 403 Access Denied or 401 on every path probed, including /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/. No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, WSDL, XSD, OpenTravel/OTA or HTNG reference is published anywhere by IHG. apis[] is deliberately empty: listing an Akamai-gated hostname or a decommissioned 2017 portal as a live API would be fabrication. The value of this record is the switchingCost block in review.yml, which captures what published IHG documents actually say about what it costs to leave — including the archived RoomService Terms of Use classing "API parameters" as Confidential Information and binding partners to the Master PartnerConnect Terms and Conditions plus the Six Continents Hotels E-commerce Master Service Agreement, and the current IHG One Rewards member terms stating that members whose accounts are cancelled "by IHG or by the Member, will forfeit all Points, Point vouchers, Reward Nights, and any other benefits associated with the account".

providers.name: TableApp
providers.description: TABLEAPP (Tableapp Sdn Bhd, part of FunNow Ltd) is a real-time restaurant discovery and reservation platform serving diners across Malaysia (Klang Valley) and Thailand. Consumers discover restaurants and book tables with instant confirmation through the TABLEAPP website and iOS/Android apps, and the TABLEAPP ELITE membership unlocks free signature dishes at partner restaurants, alongside dining vouchers and gift cards. Restaurateurs list on both TABLEAPP and FunNow and manage reservations and guest preferences with the TABLEAPP Manager tools. TableApp is a 500 Global portfolio company; it operates a private mobile-app backend (api.tableapp.com) but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: HiGuest
providers.description: HiGuests (Hi Guests Vacation Homes Rental LLC, License 765614) is a Dubai-based short-term rental property management company. It offers full-service management for vacation homes and furnished apartments, listing owners' properties across 20+ booking channels (Airbnb, Booking.com, Expedia, and others), and handling profile creation, dynamic pricing, booking and guest communications, 24/7 guest support, check-in/check-out, housekeeping, and maintenance, alongside transparent owner reporting. HiGuests markets a zero-commission subscription plan for landlords and operates a guest-facing booking site. It is a hospitality services business, not an API/developer platform; no public API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: Outsite
providers.description: Outsite is a coliving and community platform for remote workers, digital nomads, and distributed teams. It operates a global network of fully-furnished coliving spaces, curated stays, and cowork cafes across more than twenty destinations including Lisbon, Barcelona, Bali, Oaxaca, and Costa Rica, pairing dedicated coworking areas and fast WiFi with a built-in community of remote professionals. Outsite sells yearly and lifetime memberships, curated month-long Outsite Trips, and team retreat and business membership offerings for companies. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company; Outsite is a consumer hospitality and travel brand and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: Res
providers.description: Res (ResQ) is an AI-powered operations platform for the service economy, connecting restaurants, hospitality groups, and facilities-management teams with vetted trades vendors to manage repair-and-maintenance work orders end to end. The platform covers work-order intake and dispatch, vendor sourcing and communication, invoicing and payments, and reporting across trades such as HVAC, plumbing, refrigeration, and electrical. Backed by Homebrew and surfaced through the API Evangelist network, ResQ operates a web and mobile SaaS product; it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or webhook surface at this time, so this profile captures company identity, website properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Tenex
providers.description: Tenex is a PropTech platform for real estate and hospitality operators across the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region, offering an all-in-one suite that unifies property management, tenant and landlord experience, facility and asset management, real estate accounting, VR for off-plan developments, and a hospitality guest experience app. Trusted across 500+ buildings and communities, it advertises integrations with ZATCA, SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft Dynamics to automate compliance and unify operations. Tenex is backed by 500 Global and the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator. As of this enrichment pass no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface is published.

providers.name: Serve First
providers.description: Serve First is a UK-based AI-driven customer experience (CX) platform that unifies reviews, surveys, receipts, in-location feedback terminals, operational audits, and mystery shopping into a single dashboard. It turns real-time customer feedback into role-based, actionable insight, with sentiment analysis and unified reporting across retail, hospitality, facilities management, health & wellness, and franchise businesses. Serve First also provides Client Connect journey/workflow automation and Martyn's Law public-protection compliance management. Serve First does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI specification; this profile captures company identity plus verified security and compliance posture (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 via a Sprinto-hosted trust center).

providers.name: Sonder
providers.description: Sonder is a hospitality company that designs, leases, and operates a global portfolio of boutique, design-forward apartment-style accommodations and hotels for short- and extended-stay travelers. Guests book directly through Sonder's website and mobile app, where a tech-enabled experience spans contactless check-in, in-app service requests, and 24/7 local support across cities in North America, Europe, and the Middle East. In 2024 Sonder entered a long-term licensing agreement with Marriott that lists its properties in the Marriott Bonvoy program. The company is publicly traded and was backed by venture investors including Greylock. Sonder publishes no public developer API; the only machine-facing surface documented here is its responsible security-disclosure program and the site's domain-security posture.

providers.name: 86 Repairs
providers.description: 86 Repairs is a restaurant equipment repair and maintenance (R&M) management platform founded in 2018 in Chicago by Daniel Estrada and Joe Gallagher. It manages the repair lifecycle for restaurant operators — 24/7 intake and troubleshooting, warranty verification, dispatch to a vetted service provider network, preventative maintenance scheduling, equipment and asset inventory, invoice assurance and R&M spend analytics — and is used by operators and franchisees of brands including McDonald's, Wendy's, Taco Bell, Jersey Mike's, Five Guys and Wingstop. The product is delivered as an end-user web portal (portal.86repairs.com) and iOS/Android mobile apps, backed by a private NestJS service at eightysix-api.86repairs.com; it is not offered as a developer platform. Parts Town, the Addison, Illinois OEM foodservice parts distributor, acquired 86 Repairs in June 2026 to connect parts availability with repair and service workflows. As of this profile 86 Repairs publishes no public API: no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, no SDK or package on any public registry, no webhook catalog, no MCP server and no A2A agent card were found on any host it controls.

providers.name: AvantStay
providers.description: AvantStay is a technology-enabled luxury vacation rental management and hospitality company operating professionally designed short-term rental homes built for group travel across premium destinations throughout the United States. Beyond curated beachfront villas, desert estates, and mountain cabins, AvantStay runs a full-service homeowner property-management program through its Lighthouse owner portal, a 24-hour guest concierge, and a real-estate brokerage for buyers acquiring investment vacation homes. It is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass AvantStay publishes a consumer booking website and homeowner portal but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Choice Hotels
providers.description: Choice Hotels International (NYSE: CHH) is a United States hotel franchisor headquartered in North Bethesda, Maryland, operating 7,575 hotels with 656,825 rooms open across 49 states, the District of Columbia and 50 countries and territories as of December 31, 2025. Its brands include Comfort, Quality, Clarion, Sleep Inn, Econo Lodge, Rodeway Inn, MainStay Suites, Suburban Studios, WoodSpring Suites, Everhome Suites, Cambria Hotels, Ascend Hotel Collection and the Radisson Americas brands. Choice sits on the supply side of the travel distribution chain as a franchisor rather than an owner: its proprietary choiceEDGE central reservation system pushes rate, inventory and availability to ChoiceHotels.com, the Choice Privileges mobile apps, the global distribution systems (Sabre, Amadeus), the OTAs (Expedia, Booking.com) and metasearch (Kayak, Tripadvisor), while its proprietary choiceADVANTAGE property management system runs the majority of its franchised properties. API posture is honestly none-published — no public developer portal, no published API reference, no machine-readable contract, and no exit path. A TIBCO Mashery API gateway answers at api.choicehotels.com but every probed path returns ERR_596_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND, and developer.choicehotels.com is an unprovisioned Mashery CNAME returning 404 under a mashery.com certificate. All real integration is reached through gated franchisee and vendor channels (connect.choicehotels.com, choicecentral.com, the SkyTouch /CONNECT interface program) that require a commercial agreement.

providers.name: Clubessential
providers.description: Clubessential is a Cincinnati-based provider of club management software for private country, golf, city, athletic, and yacht clubs. Its cloud suite unifies club websites and mobile apps, tee-time and dining reservations, membership CRM, point-of-sale, accounting, business intelligence, and integrated payments so club staff can manage operations and member experiences from a single platform. Part of Clubessential Holdings (unified under Xplor Technologies alongside ClubReady, foreUP, Vermont Systems, PrestoSports, and Exerp), the company serves more than 1,300 private clubs and, with its sister brands, thousands of courses and clubs worldwide. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Houst
providers.description: Houst is a global short-term rental and Airbnb management company founded in 2015, operating in 17 cities across 8 countries and managing over 11,650 properties. Houst handles the full hosting lifecycle for homeowners and landlords - multi-platform listing creation and optimization, dynamic pricing, professional photography, 24/7 guest communication and vetting, check-in coordination, cleaning, linen and maintenance - powered by a proprietary host dashboard that tracks earnings, occupancy, bookings and performance. The company operates on a commission model and also runs an operating-partner and affiliate programme. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Shuttle Central
providers.description: Shuttle Central (shuttlecentral.com) is a ground transportation booking platform for airport and point-to-point shuttle transfers across Mexico, the Caribbean, the United States, and Latin America, covering 100+ destinations including Cancun, Punta Cana, Nassau, Los Cabos, Mexico City, Puerto Vallarta, Montego Bay, and Miami. Travelers book confirmed transfers online with secure payment, instant confirmation, and 24/7 support, and a separate transportation-provider program (shuttlecentralinc.com) lets ground operators sell transfers through the platform. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: EAT Club
providers.description: EAT Club is a corporate meal-delivery platform founded in 2010 in Redwood City, California by Kevin Yang and Rodrigo Santibanez, built around the idea of a "virtual cafeteria" for offices with no on-site dining. Instead of tray-style catering, each employee picks an individually packaged meal from a rotating daily menu produced by EAT Club's own kitchens and restaurant partners, and every order for a building arrives in one synchronized delivery. The company markets the program as an employee lunch benefit and reports 21 million meals delivered to roughly 1,145 companies across nine cities. Compass Group USA acquired EAT Club in October 2020 and folded its ordering, production and delivery technology into Compass Digital Labs, where it now underpins workplace, education and healthcare dining accounts across the US and Canada. The consumer-facing product is a React ordering app served from www.eatclub.com; EAT Club publishes no developer program, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: innRoad
providers.description: innRoad is a cloud-based hotel property management system (PMS) that bundles PMS, a direct booking engine, and a channel manager (OTA distribution to Expedia, Booking.com, Airbnb, and others) into one platform, built for independent hotels, boutique properties, and small hotel management companies. innRoad also offers 40+ pre-built partner connections - point-of-sale (Lightspeed, Oracle Hospitality, Squirrel, Positouch, Uniwell), door locks (RemoteLock, Saflok, ONITY), guest messaging (Akia), accounting (M3, Inn-Flow), and in-house payment processing (innRoad Payments) - that are toggled on inside the application. innRoad does NOT publish a public, self-service developer API. There is no developer portal, no public API reference, no OpenAPI definition, and no documented WebSocket or webhook API as of this cataloging; every listed integration is a pre-built, partner-gated connection rather than an open surface a third-party developer can register for and call.

providers.name: Wander
providers.description: Wander is a vertically integrated luxury hospitality company offering smart vacation homes with hotel-grade amenities, dedicated remote-work spaces, and 24/7 concierge service across North America. Founded by John Andrew Entwistle and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Wander powers owners and operators through WanderOS, its proprietary agentic AI operating system that automates dynamic pricing, operations, and guest support. The company raised a $50M Series B in 2025 co-led by QED Investors and Fifth Wall, with Redpoint Ventures, Uncork Capital, Starwood, and Breyer Capital participating, bringing total funding past $100M. Wander ships no public developer API, but publishes a deliberately agent-ready web surface: an llms.txt, an AI sitemap of 8,500+ markdown property pages with live 90-day pricing and availability refreshed daily, and Content-Signal AI-use permissions in robots.txt.

providers.name: 9flats
providers.description: 9flats is a European vacation-rental marketplace, founded in Hamburg, Germany in 2010, that lists privately-owned apartments, houses and rooms for short-term stays and takes bookings directly from travellers. It operates 9flats.com in multiple languages and, in 2016, combined with its Berlin-based competitor Wimdu. 9flats published a public read API (v1, later v3) covering place search, place detail, photos, prices, reviews, availability calendars, user profiles, favourites and bookings, authenticated with OAuth 1.0a and shipped with a first-party Ruby SDK. That developer surface has decayed: the SDK was last released in 2011 and is marked unsupported by its own maintainers, and the API reference site the SDK links to has been deleted.

providers.name: Secret Escapes
providers.description: Secret Escapes is a members-only luxury travel and holiday flash-sales platform that negotiates exclusive, time-limited discounts on hand-picked hotels, city breaks, and package holidays for its members, surfacing over 200 curated sales each week across the UK and international markets. Founded in London and backed by GV and Index Ventures, it operates on an invitation/membership model rather than a public developer platform; no public API surface is currently published.

providers.name: AiSensum
providers.description: AiSensum (AISensum) builds agentic AI "teammates" that work alongside front-line staff to drive revenue, improve quality, and reduce labour while keeping the human in the lead. Operating since 2017 with a presence across Southeast Asia, it deploys purpose-built AI teammates for enterprise front-line operations in retail, F&B, hospitality and entertainment, each specialising in one measurable outcome: Daniel (revenue teammate, personalised counter offers/upsell), Sasha (time and cost teammate, bulk product-photo editing and approval), and Nicole (progress teammate, conversation scoring and cashier coaching against brand SOPs). Deployments are scoped through a half-day IFA (Intelligent Front-line Automation) Workshop. AiSensum publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; it is a portfolio company of 500 Global tracked in the API Evangelist network. This profile was enriched from the company's public web presence and an on-site llms.txt.

providers.name: Bounce
providers.description: Bounce operates the world's largest luggage storage network, connecting travelers with more than 32,000 vetted partner locations across 4,000+ cities worldwide where they can securely drop off bags, luggage, and packages by the hour or day and explore hands-free. Founded by Cody Candee in 2018, the company runs a two-sided marketplace: travelers book storage in advance or on the spot through the Bounce web and mobile apps, while local shops, hotels, and businesses earn revenue as storage partners. Bounce also offers luggage-delivery between hotels, airports, and city locations, a hotel solutions program, and an affiliate program. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst, and Sapphire. This profile currently tracks the company's public web surface; Bounce publishes an llms.txt but no public developer API.

providers.name: Kasa Living
providers.description: Kasa Living, Inc. (operating as Kasa) is a San Francisco-founded, tech-enabled hospitality company that partners with institutional real-estate owners to convert multifamily, single-family and hotel inventory into professionally managed, apartment-style flexible accommodations across 90+ U.S. cities. Founded in 2016 by Roman Pedan, Kasa runs a proprietary hospitality operating system covering dynamic pricing, automated operations, keyless self check-in and a 24/7 remote "Virtual Front Desk" instead of an on-site front desk, and distributes inventory direct at kasa.com plus through OTAs and GDS via the NextPax supply API. Kasa publishes no public developer API, developer portal or machine-readable API specification; its one machine-readable, agent-facing artifact is a hand-authored llms.txt served at kasa.com/llms.txt.

providers.name: Lance
providers.description: Lance (Lance AI, Inc.) is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company building autonomous AI agents for hotel operations. Its platform handles guest interactions and back-of-house coordination end to end: a Receptionist agent answers guest calls, SMS, email, and hotel messaging platforms 24/7 in multiple languages, resolving questions and routing service requests; a Sales agent responds to booking inquiries and RFPs, qualifies leads, and follows up on opportunities; and Lance Pad is a tablet-based coordination surface that replaces walkie-talkies and tracks guest requests, housekeeping, work orders, and scheduling in real time. Lance reports use across brands including Marriott, Hilton, and Hyatt and more than 50 hotels, citing an 89% call success rate and a 30%+ reduction in front-desk call volume. Architecturally the company is notable for deliberately avoiding integration APIs: it uses computer-use and computer-vision agents to drive legacy property management, task, and reservation systems through their user interfaces rather than through vendor APIs. Lance is surfaced here as a portfolio company of Y Combinator. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Partender
providers.description: Partender is a bar and beverage inventory management platform that lets hospitality operators complete a full physical liquor, wine, beer, and keg inventory in roughly fifteen minutes by tap-and-swipe estimating how full each bottle is, at up to 99.2% accuracy. The subscription SaaS spans iOS, Android, and web apps and adds online ordering, purchase orders auto-sorted by distributor, pour-cost and variance reporting, and lightweight accounting so venues can cut time, labor, and inventory loss. Founded in 2012 and backed by 500 Global, Partender serves bars, restaurants, hotels, and stadiums. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Partender exposes a consumer mobile/web product rather than a publicly documented developer API.

providers.name: Jitjatjo
providers.description: Jitjatjo is a New York City based on-demand staffing and workforce management platform operated by JJJ International, matching hospitality, healthcare, education, facilities, retail and logistics businesses with W2 temporary talent in real time. The company runs two consumer-facing products — "Ondemand by Jitjatjo" for businesses booking shifts and "Flex by Jitjatjo" for talent picking up gigs — alongside "Network", a frontline vendor management system (VMS) for contingent labor that is integrated with SAP Fieldglass. JJJ International was acquired by Dayforce in September 2025 and the platform is being rebranded as Dayforce Flex Work; the Jitjatjo web apps now call API hosts on dayforceflexwork.com. Jitjatjo publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK or webhook catalog was found on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Kindred
providers.description: Kindred is a members-only home exchange platform where verified members swap their real homes with one another instead of paying for traditional accommodation. The service runs on a credit economy — members earn one night of travel credit for every night they host, and new members start with five nights of credit. Kindred verifies every member and home, provides professional cleaning before and after each stay, and includes up to $100K in damage protection. There are no membership fees; travelers pay only a cleaning and service fee per trip. The platform operates across 190+ cities in North America and Europe and is backed by a16z, Bessemer Venture Partners, GV, Index Ventures, and NEA. Kindred is a consumer travel product and does not publish a public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Onefinestay
providers.description: Onefinestay is a British luxury hospitality company founded in 2009 that curates and manages a portfolio of upmarket private homes, villas, apartments and chalets for short-term and extended vacation rentals, pairing hand-picked properties with hotel-grade concierge service. AccorHotels acquired Onefinestay in 2016 for around $168 million; in 2025 Exclusive Resorts took a controlling operational stake while Accor retained a majority interest. Onefinestay operates as a consumer travel brand with a booking website and a technical/engineering organization on GitHub, but it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK program, or developer portal. This profile is maintained as a network company record.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Ayenda
providers.description: Ayenda is a hotel-technology platform operating across Colombia, Mexico, and Peru. It combines a property management system (PMS), a channel manager for distributing hotel inventory, and a booking engine; ayenda.com is its consumer reservations channel where travelers search, compare, and book budget hotels, hostels, and aparthotels by city, neighborhood, or landmark, with both traveler and corporate (Empresas) rates.
