Its platform connects employers across hospitality, retail, industrial, care and facilities-management directly with vetted, rated temporary and part-time workers, removing the traditional recruitment agency and charging a flat fee on top of worker wages. Creandum led Syft's Series A in 2017; the company was acquired by Indeed in 2019 and now operates as part of Indeed Flex. Syft is a consumer/employer staffing marketplace and exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: TastyUrban
providers.description: TastyUrban is a Berlin-based virtual restaurant franchise and digital-first food-brand licensing company founded in 2022 by Felix Chrobog, Marc Hansell, and Gerry Pidgeon (alumni of Gorillas, Tier, and Deliveroo). It pursues an asset-light model in which existing restaurants and retail partners license and operate TastyUrban's digital food brands, using otherwise idle kitchen capacity to add revenue without major investment or operational complexity. The company is backed by Earlybird and raised a EUR 1.5M seed round in 2023 and a EUR 6.5M Series A in 2025 (led by IBB Ventures). TastyUrban operates a consumer/partner web presence at tastyurban.com but publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: The Rainmaker Group Ventures (letitrain.com)
providers.description: letitrain.com was the corporate domain of The Rainmaker Group Ventures, LLC, an Atlanta-based hospitality revenue and profit optimization software vendor serving hotels, resorts and casinos. Rainmaker sold an "intelligent profit platform" built around three products: guestrev for transient pricing and science-based revenue management, grouprev for group pricing and evaluation, and revintel for business intelligence and reporting, with a demand forecast marketed to operators including Caesars Entertainment, Atlantis Casino Resort Spa and Two Roads Hospitality. The company was backed by Norwest Venture Partners and ran offices in Atlanta, Las Vegas, Singapore and Dubai. The brand is retired: letitrain.com now serves a blanket redirect to Cendyn, the acquiring company, its TLS certificate expired in December 2022, and no Rainmaker developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification was ever published or archived. This profile is retained as a historical, defunct-provider record with no active API surface.

providers.name: Truffle
providers.description: Truffle is an AI-native restaurant operating system building "the autonomous back of house for restaurants" — one platform to manage an entire restaurant operation more profitably. The company, a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) portfolio company operating at usetruffle.ai, positions its product as an autonomous back-of-house layer that unifies the operational and administrative work that normally sprawls across separate tools. As of this profile Truffle is a very early-stage company presenting a single marketing landing page; it publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, CLI, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this API Evangelist profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture and will be re-enriched as a developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Tujia
providers.description: Tujia (途家) is a Chinese online marketplace for short-term rentals, vacation homes, and homestays, frequently described as "China's Airbnb." Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Beijing, the company connects travelers with apartments, villas, and serviced homes across China and select international destinations through its website, mobile apps, and WeChat mini-program. Tujia runs a consumer-facing booking marketplace and property-management services rather than a public developer platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; the enrichment pipeline probed the domain and found no public API, developer portal, or open platform for the company.

providers.name: VacayHero
providers.description: VacayHero (branded VaycayHero) was a vacation rental marketplace backed by a16z that offered professionally managed vacation rental homes with hotel-style guest service. The brand was absorbed by RedAwning: vacayhero.com now permanently redirects (301) to RedAwning's VaycayHero brand page, which folds the VaycayHero properties into RedAwning's collection of 100,000+ instantly bookable vacation rentals in over 10,000 destinations. VacayHero no longer operates an independent website, developer program, or public API surface.

providers.name: Yards Brewing
providers.description: Yards Brewing Company is an independent craft brewery founded in 1995 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Yards operates a brewery and taproom at 500 Spring Garden Street and distributes its classic and seasonal beers across the Mid-Atlantic. The company emphasizes local craftsmanship, community, and Philadelphia identity, summed up in their tagline that things are not made in Philadelphia but made BY Philadelphia.

providers.name: Blackbird Labs
providers.description: Blackbird Labs is a New York-based hospitality technology company building a payments and loyalty platform for restaurants and their guests. Its flagship product, Blackbird Pay, is a blockchain-powered payment network that charges restaurants roughly 2% per transaction and settles automatically at the table, while diners earn $FLY loyalty rewards by checking in and can redeem points across participating restaurants. Payments run over Flynet, a layer-three transaction protocol built on Coinbase's Base, and membership is represented by an NFC-tapped NFT. Founded by Resy and Eater co-founder Ben Leventhal, Blackbird is backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Coinbase Ventures, and Amex Ventures. Blackbird operates as a consumer mobile app and a merchant platform and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: VICI Properties
providers.description: VICI Properties is an experiential real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns one of the largest portfolios of gaming, hospitality, and entertainment destinations in the United States, including Caesars Palace and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas. The company holds long-term triple-net leases with leading gaming operators. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; VICI engages investors and partners through corporate and investor relations channels.

providers.name: BentoBox
providers.description: BentoBox is a restaurant marketing and commerce platform, part of Fiserv, that powers restaurant websites, online ordering, takeout and delivery, events, reservations, and digital presence for thousands of hospitality brands. While BentoBox runs a Technology Partners program and connects to 50+ third-party services across POS, reservations, delivery, payments, marketing, and shipping, it does not publish a public self-service developer API or API reference. Integrations are built through partnership rather than open documentation, and prospective technology partners are directed to contact the BentoBox partnerships team to integrate with the platform. As a Fiserv company, payments and commerce flows connect through Clover and Fiserv rails.

providers.name: 5Lmeet
providers.description: 5Lmeet (Chinese brand 共享际, operated by 优享创智 / UR Community) is a Beijing-based urban space operator founded in December 2015 by Dr. Mao Daqing, the former vice-chairman of China Vanke and founder of Ucommune. It runs an "urban renewal and spatial reconstruction" model that blends co-working, co-living, food and beverage, retail, fitness and cultural programming into single mixed-use compounds — the name stands for livable, linked, liberal, lively and landscape. Its Dongsi compound in Beijing pairs a basement co-working floor with a cafe and bakery, a gym, the Hatchery food incubator, the Unread bookstore, a 24-hour convenience store, residential units and a rooftop garden. The company raised roughly RMB 400 million in October 2016 and a USD 14.55 million Series B in early 2017 led by GIC, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, alongside Kaifeng Culture Tourism Investment Group, and is valued in the secondary market rather than publicly listed. 5Lmeet is a real-estate and hospitality operator, not a software vendor: the only software it has published is an end-user iPad visitor-management app for its own front desks, and it operates no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Domio
providers.description: Domio was a New York City hospitality and real-estate technology company that designed, leased, and operated branded "apart-hotels" — spacious, design-forward apartment-style accommodations aimed at group and extended-stay travelers. Founded in June 2016 by former Bank of America Merrill Lynch real-estate bankers Jay Roberts and Adrian Lam, the company used data analysis and machine learning to select buildings for its portfolio and distributed inventory through its own site and app alongside third-party channels such as Airbnb. It raised roughly $117M across five rounds, including a $12M Series A in 2018 from Tribeca Venture Partners and SoftBank Capital, a $50M joint-venture facility from Upper90, and a $100M Series B in December 2019 (half equity, half debt) led by GGV Capital with Eldridge Industries, 3L Capital, Cain International and Tenaya Capital. Airbnb suspended all of Domio's host accounts in August 2020, the co-founders resigned that September, and the company ceased operations in November 2020, selling its assets through an assignment for the benefit of creditors overseen by Sherwood Partners. Domio never published a developer program, public API, SDK, or machine-readable specification. Its former host staydomio.com was re-registered on 2021-09-19 by an unrelated party and now serves a GoDaddy parking lander, so it is deliberately not wired as a Website pointer. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Splash 360
providers.description: French vendor of point-of-sale and management software for collective catering — company restaurants, school and institutional canteens. The product line covers a smart till, self-service ordering kiosks and kiosk software, Wifi Order, a Kitchen Display System, a back-office management layer, a coin handler, and loyalty through a YouFid integration. NO PUBLIC API SURFACE: the company sells and deploys into catering operators directly, and publishes no developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable contract. That is the absence of a PUBLIC interface, not the absence of APIs — a till, a kiosk and a kitchen display exchanging orders are API-driven by construction, but those interfaces reach customers through deployment and integration work rather than a public developer program.

providers.name: Stay Alfred
providers.description: Stay Alfred Inc. was a Spokane, Washington short-term-rental and hospitality operator that pioneered the "travel apartment" — full apartments in walkable downtown cores, leased in bulk from multifamily building owners and operated with hotel-style consistency, cleaning and guest support. Founded in 2011 by Jordan Allen, who was named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year for the Pacific Northwest in 2019, the company grew to roughly 2,000-2,500 units across 28 to 33 U.S. markets including Denver, San Diego, Miami, New Orleans and Nashville, hosted around half a million guests, and employed more than 230 people. It raised approximately $62M in total venture funding, headlined by a $47M Series B in October 2018 led by Chicago real-estate technology fund Nine Four Ventures. Distribution ran through its own consumer booking site and the major online travel agencies, so Stay Alfred was an API CONSUMER rather than an API publisher; it never operated a developer program, public API, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification. COVID-19 ended it: the company closed every property nationwide from 1 April 2020, a rescue funding round was withdrawn at the last minute, and on 20 May 2020 Stay Alfred announced it would close permanently, winding down through mid-2020 while it had been on track for roughly $100M in revenue that year. The stayalfred.com domain is still on its original 2013 registration but is no longer controlled by the company: it is privacy-shielded, Cloudflare-hosted, and every path now 301-redirects into a rotating chain of unrelated third-party sites. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Gaming and Leisure Properties
providers.description: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. (NASDAQ: GLPI) is "the nation's first real estate investment trust focused on acquiring real property assets leased to gaming operators." Headquartered in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania, GLPI's portfolio comprises 71 premier gaming and related facilities across 21 states, totaling more than 29.3 million square feet and over 15,100 hotel rooms, leased on a triple-net basis to operators including Penn Entertainment, Caesars Entertainment, Bally's Corporation, Boyd Gaming, the Cordish Companies, and Hard Rock. No public developer API, data feed, or GitHub organization has been identified; GLPI engages investors, tenants, and partners through corporate and investor relations channels only.

providers.name: Darden Restaurants
providers.description: Darden Restaurants is the largest full-service restaurant company in the world, owning and operating brands such as Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Yard House, The Capital Grille, Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Eddie V's, Seasons 52, Bahama Breeze, Ruth's Chris Steak House, and Chuy's. providers.description: Life Time Group Holdings is an American health and wellness company operating large-format athletic resort destinations across the United States and Canada. The company offers fitness facilities, personal training, group classes, aquatics, indoor and outdoor sports, spa services, and healthy living programs in premium resort-style facilities, plus the Life Time app for members. Life Time does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: abcMob
providers.description: abcMob is a mobile business application company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Westminster, California. It builds and sells ready-made and custom native business applications for banking, airlines, HRIS, insurance, restaurants, hotels, tourism, universities, gyms, music, sport clubs, brokerage, oil and gas, real estate, retail, agriculture, survey, TV and places of worship. Its stated approach is to write one codebase that is translated to native code per platform (Objective-C on iOS, Java on Android, C on Windows and Linux) and compiled into full native applications, with an HTML5 web view of the same service, so the look, feel and update cadence stay consistent across devices. The company sells finished client/server applications and cloud hosting to businesses; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Textaurant
providers.description: Textaurant was an early SMS-based restaurant waitlist and table-management startup founded around 2010 by Josh Bob in Waltham, Massachusetts, and later surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. Its software let a restaurant manage its waiting list from a laptop and text guests when a table opened up, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to pager-based systems from JTECH and OpenTable. The original company is defunct: its primary domain, textaurant.com, now resolves to a parked GoDaddy "for sale" landing page with no product, documentation, or API surface. A separate, unaffiliated live app reusing the name exists at app.textaurant.app (a small Twilio-backed Next.js application served through a personal proxy), but it publishes no public API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer documentation. There is no API to onboard against; this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct provider.

providers.name: BIZZON
providers.description: BIZZON (formerly AgentCASH) was a London-based hospitality and restaurant technology company founded in 2015, offering an end-to-end point-of-sale (POS) and payments platform for the food-and-beverage and hospitality sector. Its suite spanned sales/ordering tools, business intelligence, and fully certified cloud-hosted omnichannel payment technology, letting operators manage online orders, payments, menus, inventory, staff, and loyalty. Backed by Techstars, Mews, and Ascension, BIZZON was acquired by hospitality cloud platform Mews in March 2022 and its product and infrastructure have since been folded into Mews; the former developer surface (developers.bizzon.com), status page, and the agentcash.com domain are no longer live, and the your.bizzon.com portal now redirects to pos.mews.com. This profile is retained as a historical provider/company record. No independent live API or developer surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Qlub
providers.description: Qlub is a hospitality payments and digital-menu technology company enabling contactless pay-at-table, order-and-pay, digital menus, secure payment links, a qlub SoftPOS terminal, and the qlub+ rewards program for restaurants, hotels, and hospitality venues. Diners scan a QR code to view the bill, split it, add a tip, and pay from their own phone without downloading an app or creating an account. Qlub operates globally across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, Australia, Brazil, and the United States, and integrates with more than one hundred point-of-sale systems. It is backed by Point Nine. As of this enrichment pass Qlub publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or self-serve developer portal; technical integrations are delivered through direct POS partnerships.
